headline: US electronics factory-gate prices jump 12.9%, the sharpest in the series
text:
# US electronics factory-gate prices jump 12.9%, the sharpest in the series

Seven moves, one theme: prices and volumes are being re-priced faster than the usual yearly drift, from US chip-adjacent goods to Austrian power bills.

## Today in the data

### US electronics prices break out
[US electronics factory-gate prices and chip output, yoy](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Computer and electronic producer prices rose 12.9% in the year to Aug 2026 (us-ppi-sectors), against a usual +0.63%, while machinery is up 3.9% and electrical equipment 4.4%. Chip output (us-chips) is up 11.9% in Jul 2026, worth checking against the price move. The PPI base periods differ by series, so read growth rates, not levels.

### Austrian power bills up a third
[Household electricity price, EUR/kWh, all taxes](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austria paid €0.3272 per kWh in H2 2025, up 34.3% on a year earlier and the biggest rise since the series starts in 2008 (energy-household-eu); Luxembourg, at €0.2665, is up 31.7%. Look at the dip in 2023–24 that these rises reverse: the comparison runs against subsidised bills, a base effect. Taxes and levies are included on purpose.

### Austrian pharma output halves
[Austrian industrial production by sector, 2021 = 100](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austrian pharma production was 160.4 in Jul 2026, down 45.7% on a year earlier, the sharpest fall since 2011 (eu-ipi-sectors); manufacturing overall sits at 102.6 and chemicals at 92.7. The pharma line is extremely spiky, so a single month says little about the trend. Monthly sector indices are routinely revised.

### British coal generation near zero
[UK electricity generation by source, TWh](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
UK coal generated 0.33 TWh in 2025, down 82.6% on 2024 and the sharpest fall in a record beginning in 1921 (electricity-mix). Wind, at 85.84 TWh, is now within striking distance of gas at 90.91 TWh. The last year is often Ember's provisional figure, and this is generation, not consumption.

### Estonia's car market halves
[New car registrations in Estonia by fuel](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Estonia registered 13,141 new cars in 2025, down 49% on 2024, with diesel down 70.4% to 1,738 (eu-car-registrations). Petrol, at 10,531, took most of the fall in absolute terms; battery electric is 872. Worth checking against the 2024 car-tax change; the series only starts in 2013, so "record" means twelve years.

### Hungarian mining output doubles
[Hungarian mining output, 2021 = 100](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Hungarian mining and quarrying stood at 155.7 in Jul 2026, up 101.9% on the year, the biggest rise since Sep 2018 (eu-mining-ipi). The chart shows how wide the monthly swings are in a small sector, where one site can move the index. The 2025 comparison base of 77.1 was itself unusually low.

### Egypt's FDI falls back to trend
[Egypt: net FDI inflows, current US dollars](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Egypt took in $15.45bn of net FDI in 2025, $31.1bn less than in 2024, the sharpest fall since the record starts in 1971 (macro-external). The 2024 spike is the thing to look at: the fall measures its absence. World Bank figures lag one to two years and are revised.

## Forecasts

### US electronics PPI keeps climbing
[us-ppi-sectors:computer_electronic forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last observation is 120.048 in Aug 2026 (us-ppi-sectors). The tool chose Holt-Winters additive with a 12-month period and fits the past closely, with a mean absolute error of 0.28% and residual spread of 0.42 index points. It puts Nov 2026 at 122.33, with a 95% band of 120.90 to 123.77, meaning five times in a hundred the outcome falls outside even if the pattern holds. The band assumes the recent monthly gain of about one point continues; a tariff change or a reversal in chip pricing would break it.

### Austrian pharma seen near 154
[eu-ipi-sectors:AT|C21 forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last observation is 160.4 in Jul 2026 (eu-ipi-sectors). Holt-Winters additive again, but the fit is loose: 5.5% mean absolute error and a residual spread of 13 index points. Oct 2026 comes out at 154.2 with a band of 110.2 to 198.3, a range wide enough to admit almost any plausible month, which is the honest reading of a volatile series. The next Eurostat release, due for Aug 2026, plus revisions to July, could land outside it.

### Hungarian mining flat around 151
[eu-mining-ipi:HU|B forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last observation is 155.7 in Jul 2026 (eu-mining-ipi). Holt-Winters additive, fitted with 8.7% mean absolute error, projects 151.8 for Oct 2026 within a band of 114.6 to 189.1. The band is the residual spread grown at the random-walk rate, so it widens with each step out. This is a projection of the series' own past only: a single mine reopening or closing, or Eurostat's revision of the doubled July reading, would put the outcome outside it.

## Correlations
- **US semiconductor output vs computer/electronic PPI** (yoy, 2012-01 to 2026-07, n=175): r = 0.01 at lag 0, strongest |r| = 0.14 at lag −12, not distinguishable from zero. Volumes and factory-gate prices in US electronics do not track each other at any lag here.
- **Austria vs Luxembourg household electricity** (yoy, 2008-S2 to 2025-S2, n=35): r = 0.53 at lag 0 and 0.61 at lag −1, both clear the band. The two bills move together within a half-year, consistent with a shared wholesale and tax-timing cycle rather than one country leading.

## What to watch
- **eu-ipi-sectors** (last 2026-07): the Aug reading settles whether Austrian pharma's 45.7% drop was one month or a level shift.
- **eu-mining-ipi** (last 2026-07): Aug shows whether Hungary's doubling holds above 150.
- **us-ppi-sectors** (last 2026-08): Sep tells whether electronics PPI growth is still accelerating past 12.9%.
- **cpi-eu and eu-hicp** (last 2026-08 and 2026-07): where household energy costs show up in consumer prices.
- **eu-ppi-sectors** (last 2026-08): the European counterpart to the US electronics price move.

## Sources
- us-ppi-sectors — BLS producer price indexes by NAICS industry via FRED, not seasonally adjusted, monthly; last 2026-08.
- us-chips — Federal Reserve industrial production via FRED (NAICS 3344, 334), monthly; last 2026-07.
- energy-household-eu — Eurostat nrg_pc_204, band DC, all taxes, EUR/kWh; last 2025-S2.
- eu-ipi-sectors — Eurostat sts_inpr_m, calendar and seasonally adjusted, 2021=100; last 2026-07.
- electricity-mix — Ember Yearly Electricity Data and Energy Institute, via Our World in Data; last 2025.
- eu-car-registrations — Eurostat road_eqr_carpda; last 2025.
- eu-mining-ipi — Eurostat sts_inpr_m, 2021=100; last 2026-07.
- macro-external — World Bank World Development Indicators; last 2025.
